text: Turn off your monitor when stepping away for more than 5 minutes.
explanation: Displays are some of the most power‑hungry peripherals. Turning them off during breaks can save meaningful energy over a day.

text: Enable automatic sleep mode after 10 minutes of inactivity on your laptop.
explanation: Sleep reduces CPU, disk, and display power draw to near‑idle, cutting wasted energy when you forget to close the lid.

text: Use a power strip to easily shut off multiple devices at once.
explanation: Many adapters draw standby power. A single switch eliminates vampire loads from monitors, speakers, and docks.

text: Lower your screen brightness to 50–70% to save energy.
explanation: Backlights and OLED pixels consume less energy at lower brightness, extending battery life and reducing emissions.

text: Disable keyboard backlighting when you don’t need it.
explanation: Lighting is a constant power draw. Turning it off adds up over hours of typing each day.

text: Use dark mode to reduce power on OLED screens.
explanation: OLED pixels use power per lit pixel. Dark themes reduce illuminated area, saving power on many phones.

text: Turn off Bluetooth and Wi‑Fi when not in use to reduce battery drain.
explanation: Radios periodically scan and maintain connections. Disabling them avoids background power use.

text: Close unused tabs and apps to reduce CPU load and power use.
explanation: Background pages, timers, and scripts keep processors active. Fewer tasks mean lower energy.

text: Use battery saver mode during commutes or meetings.
explanation: Battery saver throttles background syncing and visual effects to stretch battery and reduce energy.

text: Prefer wired connections when possible; they’re more energy efficient than wireless.
explanation: Wired links avoid the constant radio negotiation of wireless, reducing energy per bit transferred.
